docs.description: Three voltages that swirl around each other and never repeat, from the Lorenz attractor: organic modulation for anything that should wander without looping. Changing a param bends the path rather than restarting it.

sigma.description: how tightly the voltages chase each other: higher makes the swings snappier and more jittery, chaotic at any value above 0 (σ; the default is σ = 10, 5 is σ = 30)

rho.description: how wide and wild the swings are: higher roams further; below about 2.06 the motion settles to still voltages (ρ; the default is ρ = 28, 5 is ρ = 60)

beta.description: the shape of the loops the voltages trace; the default is the classic butterfly (β = 8/3; 5 is β = 10)

rate.description: simulation speed: 0 freezes and 5 is fastest; the default traces a slow butterfly, and from about 1.25 the chaos runs at audio rate

docs.description: The surface of a simulated sea as CV: slow rolls that bunch into sharp crests and arrive in sets, with the occasional wave far bigger than the rest. Use it for tidal filter sweeps and levels that breathe irregularly; `tilt` and `roll` are the matching lean of a boat on the water. Changing a param bends the waves rather than restarting them.

examples.title: Slow, steep swell on a filter

freq.description: rate of the main swell, e.g. `'0.1hz'`

steepness.description: crest sharpness: 0 rolls as a sine, 5 peaks into sharp crests over wide, flat troughs

chop.description: how rough the sea is: 0 is one clean, repeating swell; higher mixes in faster waves, up to `chop / 2` octaves above `freq`, so the swell rolls in sets with choppy ripples

spread.description: directional spread: 0 sends every wave the same way, 5 brings them from every direction, a confused sea

waves.description: number of waves in the sea; waves added or removed by a patch update fade over one swell period

seed.description: picks the sea: each seed, and each channel, places the waves at different frequencies and directions

SeqPatternSource.description:
Wire-level dispatch shape: a `.fast`/`.slow`/`.struct`/`.beat` wrapper, an
`$p.arrange` payload, a chained `$p.s` payload with multi-source
highlighting, or a single `ParsedPatternPayload` (the legacy single-source
path used by `$cycle($p(...))`).

The `__kind`-tagged variants are listed before the untagged `Single`; each
carries a distinct required `__kind` literal, so the untagged enum
disambiguates them unambiguously before falling back to `Single`.

FastPatternPayload.description:
JSON payload for `$p(...).fast(factor)`: speed `pattern` up by `factor`.
`pattern` is any [`SeqPatternSource`] (recursively), so `.fast` chains and
nests over `$p`, `$p.s`, `$p.arrange`, and other `.fast`/`.slow` wrappers.

__kind.description:
Discriminator — TS-side `.fast` sets this so the `SeqPatternSource`
untagged enum picks the `Fast` variant.

FastKindTag.description: Phantom discriminator matching the literal `"FastPattern"` string.

FactorPayload.description:
A `.fast`/`.slow` factor. A bare number (`.fast(2)`) is a constant speed —
not a highlightable source. A parsed pattern (`.fast("2 4")`) becomes its own
highlightable source, so its active value lights up in the editor as it
drives the speed. A non-positive factor (`0` or negative) yields silence,
matching how the in-string `*`/`/` operators lower the same factors.

anyOf.description: `.fast(2)` — a constant. JSON numbers match this before `Pattern`.

ParsedPatternPayload.description:
JSON payload shape delivered in the patch graph for
`SeqPatternParam`. Produced client-side by
the TypeScript `$p(...)` helper in `src/main/dsl/miniNotation/`.

Elements can be atoms or subpatterns.
Sequence of patterns (space-separated, played in order).

Fast subsequence from [...] syntax (explicit fastcat).
Unlike Sequence which is the implicit result of space-separated elements,
FastCat preserves that this came from explicit [...] grouping.
This distinction matters for nesting: `<[c e]>` should be slowcat of one fastcat,
not slowcat of two elements.
Slow subsequence (one item per cycle, with optional @ weight).

Replicate: pattern ! n (repeat n times).
Count is a plain u32 since Strudel doesn't support patterned replicate counts.
Degrade: pattern ? prob (randomly drop with probability).

Polymeter: `{a b, c d e}` with optional `%n` steps-per-cycle override.
Each child pattern is scaled so its step count maps to
`steps_per_cycle`; all scaled children are stacked. Default
`steps_per_cycle` is the step-count of the first child sequence.
Adapted from strudel's `polymeter` alignment in `packages/mini/mini.mjs`.

AtomValue.description:

The reduced set from strudel's krill grammar: `Number` covers bare

shorthand, sample-name identifiers, `2v` voltage, module references,
quoted strings) has been removed from the grammar and is not
representable here.

const-vs-pattern duality and is sampled at each onset; negative lengths
jump.

untagged enum picks the `Glide` variant.

ArrangePatternPayload.description:
JSON payload for `$cycle($p.arrange(...))`. Sections play in order, each for
its cycle budget; the whole loops with period `Σ cycles`. A trailing section
with `cycles == "Infinity"` loops forever once reached.

__kind.description:
Discriminator — TS-side `$p.arrange` sets this so the `SeqPatternSource`
untagged enum picks the `Arrange` variant.

ArrangeKindTag.description: Phantom discriminator matching the literal `"ArrangePattern"` string.

ArrangeSectionPayload.description:

`pattern` is any [`SeqPatternSource`] (recursively), so a section may be a
`$p`, a `$p.s`, or a nested `$p.arrange`.

SectionCycles.description:
Cycle count for an `$p.arrange(...)` section: a finite positive integer, or
the sentinel string `"Infinity"` for an infinite tail section. JSON can't
carry a numeric infinity, so the TS `$p.arrange` helper emits the string
`"Infinity"`; any finite count arrives as a JSON number.

InfinityTag.description: Phantom discriminator matching the literal `"Infinity"` string.

SpPatternPayload.description:

First entry of `sources` is the left pattern; subsequent entries are

`"squeezeout"`, `"reset"`, `"restart"`) to match the TS builder.
